newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - January 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - January 6.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
LTTE (Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam) suffer heavy losses in a battle at Kokkuthuduvai in eastern Trincomalee, rebel radio transmissions reveal, say security sources.
Student who allegedly tried to get a visa to United States using a forged marks sheet, nabbed by police.

Government to re-examine salary anomalies of public servants which exist, even after implementing the B.C. Perera Commission report. Some public servants claim recommendations of the commission do not fully adrress many issues.
Security sources say LTTE lost about 35 men in a clash at Kokkuthuduvai, while three soldiers were killed and 13 injured.
The government will do its best to get the required two-third parliamentary majority for the new constitution, says Justic Minister G.L. Peiris.
President Kumaratuga permits wife and family of slain JVP leader Rohana Wijeweera, to leave the country to reside abroad. They are now in the custody of the Sri Lanka Navy.
